2. SCD – SICKLE CELL DISEASES

•Most common inherited condition – Autosomal recessive.
•Both partner diseased = 100 % of children affected.
•Both Carrier = 25% affected, 25% (N), 50% carrier.
•One diseased one carrier = 50% affected, 50% carrier.

Includes:

•HbSS – sickle cell Anemia.
•HbSC – ed painful crises, Retinopathy.
•HbSC – combined with β Thalassemia.
•HbS – Heterozygous factors for S.
•HbAS – combined with (N) Hb – risk of UTI.

Fetal Risk: Maternal Precipitating
- Miscarriage. Risk factors for

- IUGR. - UTI Sickling Crises

- PTB - PT - NVP.

- Still Birth. - ACS - Dehydration.

- SCD – inheritance. - Painful crises - Anemia.

- VTE - Infection.

- Hypoxia.

- Cold exposure.

Pre – Conception Screening:

•Pulmonary HTN – by Echo if Not done in last 1 year.

Tricuspid jet velocity > 23 m/s indicate pulmonary HTN.

•B.P, urine analysis.
•RFT, LFT – annually.
•Retinal Screening – Pre conceptionally.
•Iron overload – Cardiac MRI if history of Transfusion or raised ferritin levels Aggressive Iron Chelation.
•Red Cell Antibodies – associated with HDFN, Delayed hemolytic Transfusion reactions in 18 – 36%.
•Genetic Screening of partner.
•Antibiotic prophylaxis penicillin/Erythromycin.
•Vaccination – Neisseria Meningitides, Strept Pneumonia, HIB, Hep B and Swine flu – yearly.
•5mg F.A in pregnancy – 1mg out site the pregnancy.
•Hydroxycarbamide – Stop 3m0 before pregnancy.

Teratogenic effects – level 3 USG is recommended if conceived With Hydroxycarbamide but Termination is not recommended unless anomaly is confirmed.

ANC:

•MDT (OBS, Midwife, Haematologist).
•Medical review if not done before.
•Avoid precipitating Factors.
•HIB vaccination.
•Antibiotic prophylaxis.
•Iron (orally if deficiency) Iron status checked regularly.
•Low dose aspirin from 12 weeks to reduce PE in all Pts with SCD.
•LMWH during hospital stay.
•B.P and urinalysis on each visit.
•Urine C/s – Monthly
• NSAIDS as relief can be given in between 12 – 28 weeks.

USG:

•7 – 9 weeks – fetal viability.
•11 – 14 weeks – Dating scan.
•20 weeks – Anomaly scan.
•4 weekly from 24 weeks – Growth Scan.

Transfusion:

•Routinely not done.
•Transfusion only if Hb <6 or 2g drop from baseline.
•Types of TX in Sickle cell disease
⇨Exchange Tx:
-Acute stroke.
-Acute chest syndrome ACS.
⇨Top – Up Tx:
-Acute anemia HB <6 OR 2g drop from baseline
⇨Prophylactic Tx:
-Twins.
-risk of painful crises so should not be given routinely.

 

Already on Tx => continue same regimen.

•Full blood count at 20, 24, 28, 32 weeks (1 monthly)

Alloimmunization = 18 – 36%.

I/P Care:

•Elective birth @ 38 weeks

ed risk of Acs, acute sickling crises in labor – more in prolong labor.

•Blood cross match – if Atypical Ab are present.
•Hospital birth – More risk of C/S.
•Keep warm and hydrated
•Keep O2 set > 94%.
•CEFM recommended because of ed risk of:
-IUGR.
-Abruption.
•Low threshold for intrapartum antibiotics.
•Avoid Pethidine, other opioids are safe
•Regional Anaesthesia is recommended
•Avoid GA – 25% more in risk of crises in GA.

 

 

PNC:

•Testing of baby (if partner is carrier or affected).
•Keep O2 sat > 94%
•LMWH:
-SVD – Hospital stay + 7 days’ post discharge.
-CS – 6 weeks post-natal.
•Stocking are recommended
•B.F is safe avoided dehydration
•Contraception:
-1st line – Progesterone containing POP, IUS, DMPA (less painful crises with DMPA).
-2nd line – Estrogen containing.

Acute painful Crises:

•25 – 50% during pregnancy.
•Urgency – Rapid assessment most frequent complication.
•Low threshold for presentation to hospital.

•MDT:
-Obstetrician
-Midwife
-Anesthetist
-Haematologist.
•Analgesia - avoid pethidine (risk of seizures)

 

Initial Analgesia should be given within 30 min

Effective analgesia within 1 hour.

•Fluid 60ml / kg / 24hrs
•O2 sats , RR, sedation level every 20 min.
•Thromboprophylaxis all women.
•NSAIDs between 12 – 28 weeks
•Morphine in severe pain (RR <10 – omit)
•Therapeutic antibiotics if needed.

 

 

Acute Complications:

•ACS – most common 7 – 20% after painful crises

Symptoms:

-Chest pain like pneumonia.
-H1N1­ – similar picture so rule out H1N1 infection.
•Stroke

Thromboprophylaxis C/I

urgent exchange Tx.

•Acute anemia – top up Tx if Hb < 6.5, or low O2 Saturation.
•Infection with Erythrovirus – Aplastic crises.
-Acute anemia.
-Fetal hydrops – FMU review due to vertical transmission.

 

 

Acute painful Crises

 

Mild Moderate Severe

- PCM - NSAID - Morphine

- Co-dydramol

- Dihydrocodeine

Monitor pain severity, RR, O2 Sat, sedation every 20 min

 

settles pain not settles in 20 min

 

Discharge Admit

 

Early pregnancy late Pregnancy

Antenatal war level II care
